primary_source_inventory:
# Live portfolio source evidence

Inspected on 17 October 2026. This ledger contains short original summaries of public source text and link destinations, not rendered observations. No screenshots, viewport checks, keyboard interactions, mobile interactions, motion checks, or performance measurements were executed. HTTP metadata and homepage link inventories are saved separately in [http-link-inventory.json](http-link-inventory.json).

The web reader and a direct HTTP client sometimes receive different responses. A reader extraction failure or HTTP 403 is recorded as an inspection limit; neither proves a broken consumer journey. Public article and repository claims are attributed to their authors, rather than independently audited. Search results from directories were used only to discover primary URLs, never to grade a designer or establish current employment.

## Paco Coursey

| ID | Primary source and ordinary path | Source observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | [Homepage](https://paco.me/) | Introduces interface/software implementation, identifies current and earlier work context, links three named software projects and Craft, and provides an explicit email address. HTTP source confirms a mailto link. |
| P2 | [Craft](https://paco.me/craft), from P1 | Groups implementation samples into motion, CSS, and interaction; each linked sample has a descriptive title and short purpose. This establishes content organisation, not visible hierarchy. |
| P3 | [Exclusion Tabs](https://paco.me/craft/tabs), from P2 | Credits the Stripe source, describes the Web Animations API and duplicated/clip-path technique, and mentions hiding duplicated items from assistive technology. Demo controls exist in fetched content; they were not operated. |
| P4 | [Command Menu](https://paco.me/craft/command), from P2 | Identifies this as the original playground that led to his library, and distinguishes a performance testing set from a larger performance goal. Neither performance claim was tested here. |
| P5 | [cmdk repository](https://github.com/pacocoursey/cmdk), from P1; resolves to [dip/cmdk](https://github.com/dip/cmdk) | README describes composable command-menu/combobox use. Its History credits Paco as the original author, Rauno for using it at Vercel, and Shu for ideas/help. Repository account ownership after a redirect is not sufficient authorship evidence by itself. |
| P6 | [next-themes](https://github.com/pacocoursey/next-themes), from P1 | A second public library destination resolves, with a concrete theming problem. Detailed code, current maintenance quality, and runtime behavior were not reviewed. |

- Search discovery initially surfaced unrelated namesakes and portfolio directories; none supplied evidence for a pass.

# Paco Coursey

**Passes — for explaining relevant implementation work in the sampled source-content screening journey.** Hypothetical target: an individual contributor who implements production web interfaces and reusable React interactions. This follows the site's introduction and linked work; it is not an inference about seniority, job-seeking status, or suitability for every role.

Inspection: [home](https://paco.me/) → [Craft](https://paco.me/craft) → [Exclusion Tabs](https://paco.me/craft/tabs) and [Command Menu](https://paco.me/craft/command); separately, home → [cmdk](https://github.com/dip/cmdk) and next-themes. The home supplies professional context and an email path. Evidence: **Source**, live HTML/text and linked README content, recorded as P1–P6 in the [ledger](.research/live-portfolios/evidence/source-ledger.md). No repository checkout or rendered page was examined. Actual motion, visible hierarchy, keyboard access, narrow layouts, and working email delivery remain unverified.

The strongest evidence is distributed sensibly across short destinations. The introduction identifies a relevant practice, the Craft examples explain implementation techniques, and the command-menu playground names its relationship to the released library. The linked README's History distinguishes original authorship, later use by Rauno, and help from Shu. That matters more than the repository's current owner or an employer name. Preserve these compact descriptions and explicit credits; a long process essay is unnecessary for this target.

There are **no confirmed source-content fixes** in this sample. The source includes both a concrete software destination and a direct mailto contact, so neither more homepage projects nor a separate résumé is justified by this review.

Remaining checks: operate the ordinary journey in a browser at desktop and narrow widths, test the command-menu controls with a keyboard, and verify that contact is discoverable in the rendered page. If the target later expands to product strategy or team leadership, that requires a separately scoped evidence review; the present samples should not be stretched into proof of those responsibilities.

Calibration: DC46 supports following a restrained shell into the work; DC136 and DM06 support specific ownership and distinguishing implementation from a broad design-engineering title.

# Emil Kowalski

**Passes — for the sampled source-content screen for reusable interface implementation.** Hypothetical target: a design engineer who builds and refines React components for designers and developers. This is grounded in the site's own positioning and projects. No leadership level or job search is inferred.

Inspection: [home](https://emilkowal.ski/) → [Sonner](https://sonner.emilkowal.ski/) → its documented usage; home → [toast](https://emilkowal.ski/ui/building-a-toast-component) and [drawer](https://emilkowal.ski/ui/building-a-drawer-component) build essays, plus GitHub. Evidence: **Source**, E1–E5 in the [ledger](.research/live-portfolios/evidence/source-ledger.md). The library demos and source code were not run or audited. Motion quality, keyboard operation, touch behavior, accessibility, and responsiveness remain unverified.

This sample connects the role claim to named software, a package interface, and explanations of decisions. The toast essay explains interruptible motion, API ergonomics, and behavior when attention moves to another tab. The drawer account explains drag/scroll conflicts and input constraints, and identifies the Radix foundation. The toast account also credits inspiration from react-hot-toast. These specifics provide reasoning and authorship evidence without needing adoption figures or employer prestige. Preserve the project-first path, API examples, and account of compromises.

There are **no confirmed source-content fixes**. Course promotion does not, by itself, obscure the projects in the fetched content. No ordering or visibility defect can be inferred from the extraction alone. A separate taste page or a longer process narrative is unnecessary.

Remaining checks: operate the demos and project-return path in a browser, including touch-compatible controls and reduced motion where relevant, and confirm rendered access to a professional contact route. The drawer essay describes work at a historical development stage; it should not be used to assert the library's current maintenance status. No supplied claim that Radix guarantees accessibility was adopted as our own runtime conclusion.

Calibration: DC36 and DC46 support inspecting actual work; DM01 and DM06 support evaluating reasons and responsibilities instead of tool fluency alone.

The introduction and linked work support this scope. This is not a conclusion about design leadership or ownership of all Notion AI work.

No app, CLI, agent, keyboard flow, viewport, or contact interaction was executed.

Shiori explains a concrete save-and-retrieve task, but its marketing page alone would not establish authorship. The linked personal account explicitly identifies it as a side project Brian shipped. HN CLI documents a bounded reader and explains story/comment limits in relation to attention. The recent model-picker account adds a specific contribution claim and user difficulty without claiming sole ownership of a team product. App Dissection is clearly analysis of other people's work. Preserve these distinctions and the variety of actual software destinations.

# Jessica Hische

**Passes — for source-content screening of a specialist brand/lettering contributor.** Hypothetical target: an individual contributor creating custom lettering and logo work for commercial brands. The site explicitly supports commissions, so the review respects that commercial purpose. It does not impose a job-seeking CV or infer product-management ability from entrepreneurship.

Inspection: [home](https://jessicahische.is/) → [Logos & Logo Refreshes](https://jessicahische.is/makinglogos), [Audible](https://jessicahische.is/working/Books/Audible-Pride-and-Prejudice), [Hallmark](https://jessicahische.is/working/Miscellany/Hallmark), and [About](https://jessicahische.is/anoversharer); additional project-route checks for Jonathan Gold and Starbucks. Evidence: **Source**, J1–J7 in the [ledger](.research/live-portfolios/evidence/source-ledger.md). Text extraction and linked image references were inspected, not the actual images. The reader succeeded where direct HTTP returned 403. A failed Commissions extraction was not reproduced in a browser.

The specialty is explicit, the work is named, and short descriptions carry useful decisions. Audible distinguishes her lettering/feather contribution, art direction, texture help, and a hierarchy adjustment for the voice artist. Hallmark connects a keepsake intention to a physical design and production techniques, while crediting art directors. These accounts answer contribution and judgment without a conventional product-design case study or business metrics. Preserve the collaborators and concise explanations.

There are **no confirmed source-content fixes** for this scope. A gallery-led brand specialty does not require a reusable software tool to count as work. Client and award lists add context but do not supply the reasons for this pass. Multiple inquiry destinations are present in source, although actual sending and rendered discoverability were not tested.

Remaining checks: inspect the artifacts to judge lettering, typography, composition, and production evidence; verify category/project navigation, return paths, inquiry links, keyboard access, and narrow layouts. This pass establishes that the sampled content explains relevant work well enough for an initial conversation. It does not certify visual craft without looking at the work, nor transfer specialist evidence into an unrelated general-product or leadership role.

Calibration: DC182 supports valuable specialist depth, DC136 supports contribution clarity, and DM07 allows a client-oriented portfolio to retain its own purpose and voice.

limits: One reviewer, established-designer convenience sample, provisional roles inferred from site content; no control group or hiring-outcome measurement.
Fetched primary text and HTML only. No browser, inspected pixels, keyboard, mobile, performance, contact sending, app execution, or accessibility verification.
Snapshot predates Design Discipline, Hiring Humans, and video additions; this is an exploratory application of the prior candidate, separate from synthetic regression runs.
Full frozen snapshot, HTTP inventory, and raw research remain locally under .research/live-portfolios/.
